newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik soldiers killed in fighting with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Tajik soldiers killed in fighting with rebels.

text.p: Tajikistan's Islamist opposition said it had taken control of the town of Garm on Sunday after fierce clashes with Tajik government troops.

"Garm came under opposition control in the second half of the day," Jaloleddin Makhmudov, an opposition official and a member of a United Nations ceasefire commission based in the capital Dushanbe, told Reuters by telephone.
The Tajik government said four of its soldiers had been killed when opposition guerrillas stormed administrative buildings in Garm on Sunday. There was no word on opposition casualties.
"Full responsibility for this lies with the (Tajik) opposition," said a statement by the interior and security ministries issued to journalists.
Itar-Tass news agency said about 100 rebels had attacked administrative buildings in Garm, setting some of them ablaze. It added that the Dushanbe authorities had sent reinforcements to the region.
Communications with the region, some 200 km (130 miles) to the east of the capital of the former Soviet republic, had been severed and the reports could not be independently confirmed.
Tajik government troops, backed by the Russian military, have fought the Islamist opposition in the remote, impoverished republic bordering Afghanistan and China for nearly five years.
The guerrillas operate out of bases inside Afghanistan and control more than half the country, mainly sparsely populated mountainous territory in the east.
The fighting erupted just days before talks planned for December 9 between embattled Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri in northern Afghanistan.

The opposition was also widely held to have carried out attacks on Russian soldiers in the capital Dushanbe earlier this month. A United Nations-sponsored ceasefire is routinely flouted by both sides.

A complex web of regional and clan rivalries underlies the struggle between the secular government and Islamist guerrillas in a bitter civil war which has killed tens of thousands and displaced many more among the population of 5.7 million.
